questions.text: Compare quality pass rates across Milwaukee, Detroit, and Cedar Rapids. Which plant has the most failures and are any linked to the same product specification?
Which customer orders are at risk of missing their delivery date? Cross-reference order due dates with current production run status and line availability.
Which production lines have critical or high-priority maintenance work orders open right now across all three plants? Show the asset, priority, and current line status.

Take the 10 most recent production batches with failed quality checks. Which suppliers' material lots went into them? Count those batches per supplier, worst first, and give one example batch with its failure for each.
Which production runs have quality checks that deviate from the engineering specification? Show the spec tolerance, actual measurement, and which product revision was in effect.
Which equipment has caused the most production downtime this week? Cross-reference maintenance work orders with production run interruptions to identify the root cause.
Show the top 5 open customer orders by value from ERP, with the customer company name, order status, and total amount.

Pick one shipment that was delivered in the last 7 days and tell me the other customer company names who received product from that same batch, the suppliers who supplied the raw materials for that batch, and which production line and MES work order produced it.
For the 5 most recently completed Milwaukee work orders, which ERP material lots and suppliers went into them? Show work order, lot number, supplier and any failed quality checks.
What is the employee turnover rate at each plant for the last quarter?
Show me the most recent CMMS work orders with their full descriptions, and summarize any unusual notes.

AnyCompany Drivetrain Assembly says the Precision Shaft 7742 parts they received over the past 7 days have out-of-tolerance bores. Which production batches did their shipments come from, and did any of those batches fail inspection at the Indianapolis plant?

hints.must_not_scope: a denial counts only when it names the failed run itself or denies every batch; the customer's other batches may honestly pass

questions.text: Which customers received parts from batch {run} or from any other batch made from the same material lot? Give the units each customer received, the value of those parts, and the total.

hints.note: Module 7b lot total, the figure an external client (AWS Quick) receives through the query bridge. Line values, not invoice values. The run is named the way the module page has the attendee paste it (the run number from module 2, suffix -90001), filled from this account's story answer key.

questions.text: Was machine L3-M1 maintained on schedule before production run {run} ran?

hints.note: Module 5 step 1, asked after module 4 onboards the plant CMMS. The question names the plant MES machine id only; the CMMS answers under its own asset tag. The page's answer: not on schedule, the deferred spindle-bearing PM PM-1001-0007 (work order 3101) on asset 1001-CMX-441. Guards the deletion of the registration identity sentences: the tag has to reach the CMMS call from the graph.

questions.text: Is vibration on the CMX-441 trending up over the last hour, and which current work orders and open shipments are at risk if it fails?

hints.note: Module 6 step 2, after module 4. One answer from four systems: SiteWise vibration, the plant MES work order on line 3 (or that line 3 is idle), the CMMS PM 3101 / PM-1001-0007, and ERP orders or shipments of the part the machine builds. The question names the machine designation only; the MES and CMMS each keep the machine under another identifier.
